testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab because of:

options.text: Using the wrong type of fuel.
Not enough oil in the engine.
Tires that are not fully inflated.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous. It can let poisonous fumes into the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: When should you turn off a retarder for safety?

options.text: When the roads are wet, snowy, or icy
When you are carrying a passenger
When you are carrying a heavy load

questions.correctAnswerText: When the roads are wet, snowy, or icy
questions.explanation: A retarder helps slow your vehicle and reduces brake use. But it can cause wheels to slip when there is poor traction. Turn off the retarder on wet, snowy, or icy roads.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park the vehicle
To stop the vehicle while driving normally

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park the vehicle
questions.explanation: Use the parking brake every time you park your vehicle.

questions.question: Vehicles with dual air brake systems:

options.text: Have air pressure in the brakes even when the engine is off.
Keep some air pressure in the brakes when the engine is off.
Must run the engine to build air pressure so the brakes work.
Keep air pressure when shut off for less than four hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must run the engine to build air pressure so the brakes work.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, run the engine to let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi of pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: When are most drivers the least alert?
questions.explanation: Fatigue and reduced alertness are serious dangers at night. Most people are least alert at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: Water and compressor oil are often found in compressed air inside air brake systems. What should be done with them?

options.text: They are needed for the brakes to work properly.
Add more if the level is low.

questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems contains water and compressor oil. If they build up, they can damage the brakes. Open the manual air tank drains every day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Allow rainwater to enter the air tanks.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains that let water and compressor oil be removed from the system. If water and oil build up, they can damage the air brake system.

questions.question: When entering traffic, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Wait for a large gap between vehicles.
Know that your vehicle will accelerate slowly, especially if loaded.
Make sure you can fully cross traffic without getting in the way.
Assume other drivers will make room for your large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers will make room for your large vehicle.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic, remember how large your vehicle is and how much space it needs to speed up. Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle before you accelerate. If your vehicle is heavily loaded, you will need even more space. Be sure you can cross the road completely without getting in the way of traffic.

questions.question: After you stop during the stop/start maneuver, you should:

options.text: Not use four-way flashers since it is only a test, not an emergency.
Leave the vehicle in first gear.
Park in front of a fire hydrant.

questions.explanation: When you stop during the stop/start maneuver in the driving skills test, turn on the four-way flashers and shift into neutral or park. Do not block driveways, intersections, fire hydrants, or signs.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks are in an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. The number and size of tanks in an air brake system differs from vehicle to vehicle.

questions.question: If your hydraulic pressure fails, which action should you NOT take?
questions.explanation: If your brakes lose hydraulic pressure, downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Look for an escape route like an escape ramp, open field, or side street.

questions.question: What are passive railroad crossings?

options.text: Crossings with no traffic control devices.
Crossings with gates that lower when trains approach.
Crossings that large trucks should never use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossings with no traffic control devices.
questions.explanation: Passive crossings have no traffic control devices. The driver alone decides whether it is safe to cross.

questions.question: Heavy steering often means:
questions.explanation: Heavy steering usually means a front tire has failed. If steering feels different, pull off the road safely and check your tires right away.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Leave the keys in the ignition.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for an ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check for ABS, look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires at the back of the brakes.

questions.question: When exiting a bus during the skills test, you must:

options.text: Keep both hands on the handrail.

questions.explanation: When exiting during the skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. On a bus, hold the handrail firmly. Exiting incorrectly will result in automatic failure.

questions.question: What do headers do?

options.text: Protect the driver during a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver during a crash.
questions.explanation: Front-end headers protect the driver from cargo moving forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: For an air brake leakage test on a single vehicle, what is the maximum air loss allowed?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 3 psi of air in one minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: In newer vehicles with air brakes, how do you apply the parking brake?

options.text: Pull out a diamond-shaped yellow knob.
Pull out a round red knob.
Pull out a square green knob.
Pull out a black round knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull out a diamond-shaped yellow knob.
questions.explanation: The parking brake in newer air brake vehicles is a diamond-shaped yellow knob. Pull it out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: During the skills test, if you must stop before turning, you should:

options.text: Stop past the stop line for a better view.

questions.explanation: Stop smoothly behind any stop line or sign. Keep your front wheels straight and do not let your vehicle roll. Stop where you can still see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What is the smallest size a placard can be?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be diamond-shaped and at least 10 ¾ square inches in size.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: To stop normally in a vehicle with air brakes, press down on the brake pedal.

questions.question: A 40-foot item on a flatbed trailer needs at least ____ tie-down(s).
questions.explanation: Cargo on a flatbed trailer needs one tie-down for every 10 feet of length. All cargo must have a minimum of two tie-downs, no matter the size.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in a school zone when children are present, unless posted otherwise?
questions.explanation: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit in school zones where children are present is 15 mph. Always drive carefully near children and pedestrians.

questions.question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Take your foot off the brake pedal.
Turn quickly toward the direction of the skid.

questions.explanation: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, take your foot off the brake pedal so the wheels start rolling again. Turn quickly in the direction you want to go, then countersteer to prevent the vehicle from skidding the other way.

questions.question: How do you use the stab braking method?

options.text: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until they roll again, then repeat.
Press the brakes halfway and keep the wheels rolling.
Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock and the vehicle stops.
Use the emergency brake until the vehicle slows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until they roll again, then repeat.
questions.explanation: Stab braking for emergency stops means fully pressing the brakes until they lock. Release the brakes until the wheels roll, then repeat the process.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, the oil pressure should:

options.text: Slowly build up over a few minutes.
Reach normal level within a few seconds.
Start high, then drop quickly while running.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reach normal level within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, oil pressure should reach a normal level within seconds. Do not drive if the oil pressure is low, dropping, or changing.

questions.question: Too little weight on a steering axle causes:
questions.explanation: Cargo weight must be balanced so the vehicle handles safely. If cargo is too far back, the front axle becomes too light and the front wheels may not have enough grip for safe steering.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: While driving, look ahead to spot hazards early. Plan how you will handle dangerous situations if they develop.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, what is the maximum air loss for a triple combination vehicle?
questions.explanation: Know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A triple combination vehicle should not lose more than 6 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in how much time?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems. This takes about 45 seconds.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, what should the driver do?
questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers. This warns other drivers that you are there.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Stop a vehicle from speeding uphill
Stop a vehicle from speeding downhill

questions.explanation: Anti-lock braking systems (ABS) prevent your wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph under good conditions needs approximately how many feet to stop?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes thinking time, reaction time, brake delay, and actual braking. An air brake vehicle going 55 mph needs about 450 feet to stop completely under ideal conditions.

questions.question: If you realize you may be late, what should you do?

options.text: Use flashing lights to make other drivers move
Drive safely and arrive when you arrive

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive safely and arrive when you arrive
questions.explanation: Do not drive dangerously because you are late. Stay calm and accept delays. Plan extra time before you leave so you are not rushed.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, what pressure must build up in both systems?
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the air compressor build pressure to at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the drinks were consumed

questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration depends on three things: how much alcohol you drink, how quickly you drink it, and your body weight. Drink temperature does not matter.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times
Push in the brake control knob

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: In newer air brake vehicles, a yellow diamond-shaped knob controls the parking brake. Pull it out to set the brake and push it in to release it.

questions.question: At dawn or dusk, how can you help other drivers see you better?
questions.explanation: At dawn, dusk, and in snow or rain, turn on your headlights. This makes your vehicle easier for other drivers to see.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum total weight allowed for a vehicle and its cargo
The minimum weight allowed for a trailer
The maximum weight allowed for a trailer and its cargo
The maximum weight allowed for only a tractor

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum total weight allowed for a vehicle and its cargo
questions.explanation: The Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum combined weight of a vehicle plus its load that the manufacturer allows.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to do which of the following?
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be:
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers and trailers without sides must be securely tied down. This keeps it from shifting or falling off during transport.

questions.question: When turning quickly to avoid an object in the road, you should:

options.text: Apply your brakes as you steer.
Give yourself extra clearance by turning more than needed to miss the object.
Turn just enough to miss the object and avoid turning more.
Steer and accelerate at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just enough to miss the object and avoid turning more.
questions.explanation: Turn only as much as needed to clear the object. Do not apply the brakes while turning.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, the landing gear should be:

options.text: More worn on the passenger's side than on the driver's side.

questions.explanation: During a trailer inspection, make sure the landing gear is fully raised. Check that no parts are missing, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame is not damaged.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle, you should:
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: When stopping, the brake pedal should be:
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down slowly. Control the pressure so your vehicle stops safely and smoothly.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, what can you do to reduce braking?
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before going down a hill. This helps your vehicle maintain a safe speed without using the brakes too much.

questions.question: When traction is poor, a driver should accelerate slowly to:

options.text: Because it is always best to accelerate slowly.
Avoid losing control of the vehicle.
Not accelerate faster than the vehicle ahead.
Be the last vehicle through an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up too quickly on a slippery road can cause you to lose control. In poor traction conditions, accelerate slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: When an engine starts, what should happen?

options.text: Warning lights should come on and then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights should come on and then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: After starting, warning lights and buzzers should turn off after a few seconds. If they do not turn off, there may be a problem with the vehicle.

questions.question: The main reason to inspect your vehicle before a trip is:

options.text: To wake up before the drive.

questions.explanation: The main reason to inspect your vehicle before a trip is to ensure safety for yourself and others on the road. Vehicle safety inspections before each trip are required by state and federal laws.
